units.content: Proposed empirical framework for identifying historical transitions from ordinary adaptation toward adaptive acceleration; asks whether measurable generator changes predict later capability acceleration.
Transformation Event: historical intervention believed to change how a system produces future states.
Possible G_m proxies: iteration-cost reduction, accessible-approach expansion, representation compression, reusable infrastructure, improvement automation.
Proposes reachable-space proxy families and Omega_hat=Delta(Delta C/Delta G_m)/Delta t as operational approximation.
Each event should record t_Gm, t_Omega, t_C; predicted ordering t_Gm<t_Omega<t_C.

content.resource_dominated_growth: C grows with resource contribution dominating

units.content: Identify event -> measure generator change -> estimate reachable-space expansion -> measure Omega -> compare capability outcomes; required controls separate resource, capability and generator effects.
Directory is for empirical designs, datasets, benchmarks and analyses; purpose is not to demonstrate correctness but test operationalization and comparison with alternatives.
Does improvement of capability-generation machinery precede measurable capability acceleration?
Experimental target is Delta G_m->Delta Omega->Delta C ordering historically and experimentally.
System -> intervention -> Delta G_m -> Delta Omega -> Delta C, with explicit steps identifying system/intervention, estimating G_m and Omega, and comparing delayed capability growth.
Possible generator proxies include Delta L, Delta A, Delta I and Delta T.
Target Omega uses generator contribution to reachable expansion; operational approximation Omega_hat=Delta(Delta C/Delta G_m)/Delta t.

Identify whether observed capability growth comes from resources, existing capability improvement, or generator mechanisms; target Omega=Delta_G.
Delta C alone is insufficient evidence; causal question asks whether improvement machinery creates disproportionate future gains relative to resource scaling.
Defines generator intervention effect as future-capability contrast C_future(G_m+Delta G_m)-C_future(G_m), equivalent to Y(1)-Y(0).
Control resource changes, existing capability and environmental changes; compare matched systems differing in G_m.
Proposes difference-in-differences model with system/time fixed effects and generator term; beta>0 would support generator-modification predictive claim.
Proposes event-study design around identifiable generator transition t0 and delayed G_m->Omega->C sequence.
Proposes instrumental-variable strategy requiring relevance and exclusion; source explicitly says this is difficult but theoretically possible.
Proposes weaker temporal Granger test and mediation structure G_m->Omega->C with positive coefficients.
Changes in mechanisms producing innovation are proposed as measurable causal precursors of capability acceleration.
Measures latent generator modification capacity G_m through observable evidence; G_m is not intelligence/capability/knowledge/output quality/resources.
G_m exists when system can change G_s(t) into G_s(t+1): method-production process changes, not merely execution.
Better execution may raise C while G_m≈0; better method creation is generator improvement.
Practical estimator G_m_hat=(Delta T,Delta A,I_r,A_m,Delta L,eta_s,SM); source explicitly states no single proxy is sufficient.

Normalize against compute, energy, capital, labor and data; G_m != R.
